_doc: Machine-readable manifest of EVERY configurable env surface in seneschal — the single source
the /setup wizard's env walker, the doctor, and setup_env.py/setup_state.py read. Tracked;
contains no secrets (only variable NAMES, defaults, and validation shapes).
Entry fields: id (manifest id; the wizard's chapter is 'env:<id>'), title, required (core
channel vs optional), enable_question (the wizard's opt-in question; null when required or
owned elsewhere), format ('env' = KEY=VALUE file rendered from the example by setup_env.py;
'json' = a JSON config copied/edited by its owning chapter — var parity checks don't apply),
path (the real, gitignored file), example (the tracked template; always path + '.example'),
docs (the setup walkthrough), depends[] (string dep id, or {id, soft, why} — soft deps degrade
gracefully instead of blocking), notes[], vars[], post[] (follow-up steps after the file is
written), verify {cmd, expect, user_confirm?} (a REAL command; '{path}' expands to the entry's
path; success = exit 0 AND expect appearing in stdout; user_confirm = a human must confirm the
out-of-band effect), ollama_models[] (models to `ollama pull` for this feature), handled_by
(a non-env chapter owns writing this file; listed here for doctor completeness),
vars_complete (false + vars_incomplete_reason exempts an entry from bidirectional var parity).
Var fields: name, required, secret (never echo/log/store its value — errors say <redacted>),
default (vanilla value; may reference another var as '{VAR_NAME}', expanded at render time),
prompt (wizard question), validate (Python re.fullmatch pattern applied to provided values),
discover {say, cmd, extract} (how to find the value when the owner doesn't know it).
Known dependency ids: proton-bridge-running (Proton Mail Bridge installed + signed in),
venv-websockets (the uv venv's websockets package), ollama (local Ollama server, vanilla
http://localhost:11434), worker:deployed (the phone/ call-screener Worker deployed).
Ordering contract: required entries precede optional ones (CI-enforced by test_env_manifest.py).

entries.title: Telegram bot — the core chat + push channel
notes: No inline '# comment' after a value — everything after '=' is the value.
TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS is strongly recommended — usually just TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID.
The verify sends a real message to the owner's chat, so it doubles as the end-to-end test.

vars.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
vars.prompt: Bot token from @BotFather (looks like 123456789:AA...)

vars.name: TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
vars.prompt: Your chat id with the bot (the default recipient for pushes/replies)

discover.say: Message the bot once (any text) so the Bot API has an update to read, then run the discover command and read chat_id from the output.

vars.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS
vars.prompt: Inbound allowlist (comma-separated chat ids; strongly recommended — usually just your own chat id)

vars.name: TELEGRAM_PARSE_MODE
vars.prompt: Default outbound parse mode ('' plain is safest, or MarkdownV2 / HTML)

vars.name: TELEGRAM_API_BASE
vars.prompt: API base override (proxy/test harness only — keep the default)

verify.cmd: python seneschal/scripts/telegram_send.py --env-file {path} --text "Seneschal setup: Telegram is connected."
verify.user_confirm: Did the message arrive in your Telegram chat with the bot?

entries.title: Proton Mail Bridge — the assistant's own email address
entries.enable_question: Should the assistant have its own email address via Proton Mail Bridge (send + read)?

depends.why: the credentials come from Bridge's Mailbox details, and verify logs into Bridge's local IMAP

notes: GOTCHA: no inline '# comment' after a value — everything after '=' becomes the value, so an added comment silently corrupts the password.
Use the Bridge-GENERATED mailbox password (~24 chars) from Bridge -> Mailbox details, NOT the Proton login password.
Username is EXACTLY what Bridge shows — often the PRIMARY account address, not the assistant's alias.
Without this file, email-triage falls back to Gmail (draft-only).

vars.name: PROTON_BRIDGE_USER
vars.prompt: Bridge mailbox username (from Bridge -> Mailbox details; usually the primary account address)

vars.name: PROTON_BRIDGE_PASS
vars.prompt: Bridge-generated mailbox password (from Bridge -> Mailbox details)

vars.name: PROTON_SMTP_HOST
vars.prompt: SMTP host (keep the default unless Bridge shows another)

vars.name: PROTON_SENDER
vars.prompt: The From address the assistant sends as (the assistant's alias; defaults to the bridge user)

vars.name: PROTON_SMTP_INSECURE
vars.prompt: Accept Bridge's local self-signed cert (keep 1 unless you've installed Bridge's CA)

entries.title: Google (Calendar + Gmail) REST bridge
entries.enable_question: Connect Google Calendar + Gmail (reads/drafts are act-low; sending stays draft-and-hold)?
notes: One Cloud 'Desktop app' OAuth client serves ALL accounts; per-account refresh tokens land in seneschal/state/google_tokens.json (gitignored).
Publish the OAuth consent screen to 'In production' or refresh tokens expire after 7 days.
No inline '# comment' after a value — the whole line after '=' is the value.

vars.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
vars.prompt: OAuth client ID (Cloud console -> Credentials -> OAuth client ID, type Desktop app)

vars.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
vars.prompt: OAuth client secret (same Cloud console credential)

vars.name: GOOGLE_SCOPES
vars.prompt: Space-separated OAuth scopes (blank = the default calendar + gmail set)

vars.name: GOOGLE_TOKEN_STORE
vars.prompt: Refresh-token store path (blank = seneschal/state/google_tokens.json)

vars.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_PORT
vars.prompt: Fixed loopback port for the consent flow (blank = pick a free port)

post: Run the one-time per-account consent: python seneschal/scripts/google_auth.py --env-file {path} --account <label>  (opens a browser; the loopback redirect completes it). Repeat per account label.

entries.title: Discord bot — second two-way chat surface
entries.enable_question: Add Discord as a second two-way chat surface (same persona as Telegram)?

depends.why: gateway websocket push inbound needs the uv venv's websockets; without it inbound degrades to REST polling (outbound unaffected)

notes: Enable Developer Mode in Discord settings to copy channel/user ids (right-click -> Copy ID).
The daemon auto-detects discord.env once present (--no-discord opts out); no other wiring needed.

vars.name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
vars.prompt: Bot token from the Discord Developer Portal (Bot -> Reset Token)

vars.name: DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID
vars.prompt: The private channel id the assistant posts in and watches

vars.name: DISCORD_ALLOWED_USER_IDS
vars.prompt: Allowlist of author ids allowed to drive the assistant (comma-separated; set your own user id)

vars.name: DISCORD_API_BASE
vars.prompt: API base override (proxy/test only — keep the default)

entries.title: Front-door Router advisor (local Ollama classifier, shadow mode)
entries.enable_question: Enable the local front-door router (needs Ollama; phase-1 shadow classifier, log-only)?

depends.why: the classifier runs on a local Ollama model; at runtime an unreachable Ollama abstains to 'escalate' (safe), but the feature does nothing without it

notes: All vars have safe defaults baked into router.py — router.env is optional; write it only to override.
Phase 1 is shadow-only: verdicts are logged to state/router-log.jsonl, behavior unchanged.
Verify caveat: with Ollama down the router abstains to 'escalate' instead of failing, so the verify passes either way — the doctor's 'ollama' dependency probe is the real reachability check.

vars.name: OLLAMA_URL
vars.prompt: Where the local Ollama server listens

vars.name: ROUTER_MODEL
vars.prompt: The local classifier model

vars.name: ROUTER_CONF_THRESHOLD
vars.prompt: Minimum confidence to accept a 'trivial' verdict (below = escalate)

verify.cmd: python seneschal/scripts/router.py "setup smoke: remind me to stretch"

entries.title: Local semantic RAG index (Retrieval advisor, phase B)
entries.enable_question: Enable the local semantic memory index (needs Ollama; additive — falls back to store search without it)?

depends.why: embeddings come from a local Ollama model; at runtime Retrieval falls back to store search when Ollama is absent, but the index can't build without it

notes: All vars have safe defaults baked into rag_common.py — rag.env is optional; write it only to override.
Verify succeeds (exit 0) only once the index has content — run the post steps first; an empty index prints [] and exits non-zero by design (the fallback signal).

vars.name: OLLAMA_URL
vars.prompt: Where the local Ollama server listens

vars.name: EMBED_MODEL
vars.prompt: The local embedding model

vars.name: CHUNK_CHARS
vars.prompt: Target chars per chunk

vars.name: CHUNK_OVERLAP
vars.prompt: Overlap between chunks

post: Optional project-state layer (interactive): copy seneschal/state/project-roots.example.json to seneschal/state/project-roots.json and set the roots to scan.
Build the initial index: python seneschal/scripts/rag_index.py --local

entries.title: Offline sentiment cross-check (salience Phase 2)
entries.enable_question: Enable the offline sentiment cross-check for forgetting events (needs Ollama; abstains to neutral without it)?

depends.why: the scoring model runs on local Ollama; at runtime an absent Ollama abstains to neutral (weight 0.0) — a cross-check, never a hard dependency

notes: Shares qwen3.5:4b with the router — one `ollama pull` covers both.
All vars have safe defaults baked into sentiment.py — sentiment.env is optional.
Verify caveat: with Ollama down the classifier abstains (weight 0.0) instead of failing — the doctor's 'ollama' dependency probe is the real reachability check.

vars.name: OLLAMA_URL
vars.prompt: Where the local Ollama server listens

vars.name: SENTIMENT_MODEL
vars.prompt: The local scoring model

verify.cmd: python seneschal/scripts/sentiment.py "thanks, this helped a lot"

entries.title: Home Assistant REST API (presence Phase 5 device control)
entries.enable_question: Connect Home Assistant for presence-driven device control (act-high; every automation stays draft-and-hold until approved)?
notes: Inert until this file exists AND each automation is individually approved; failsafes stay ask-high always.
Create the token: HA -> your profile -> Long-Lived Access Tokens -> Create Token.
ha_client has no smoke CLI, so verify is a python -c import + config-presence check; a real HA service call is act-high and belongs to the owner.

vars.name: HA_URL
vars.prompt: Your HA base URL (e.g. http://homeassistant.local:8123, or a LAN/tailnet IP:8123)

vars.name: HA_TOKEN
vars.prompt: Long-lived access token (HA -> your profile -> Long-Lived Access Tokens)

post: Copy seneschal/state/presence-automations.example.json to seneschal/state/presence-automations.json and define your context-edge -> service-call automations (each stays draft-and-hold until explicitly approved; failsafes stay ask-high).

verify.cmd: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'seneschal/scripts'); import ha_client; print('ha_client ok; configured:', ha_client.available())"

entries.title: Outbound phone calls (Call Me reminders via the call-screener Worker)
entries.enable_question: Enable can't-miss phone-call reminders (requires the phone/ call-screener Worker deployed)?

depends.why: the Worker endpoint must exist and PUSH_CALL_SECRET must be set on it (wrangler secret put) before this env can work

notes: If the Worker isn't deployed yet, mark this chapter blocked and move on — deploying the Worker (cd phone && wrangler deploy) is its own task, not an inline step of the env walker.
Twilio creds stay in Cloudflare; only the Worker URL + bearer secret live here.
Verify is a --dry-run (no network, no ring); a live test call is owner-initiated.

vars.name: PUSH_CALL_URL
vars.prompt: Full endpoint URL of the deployed Worker (include /push-call)

vars.name: PUSH_CALL_SECRET
vars.prompt: The bearer secret matching `wrangler secret put PUSH_CALL_SECRET` on the Worker

vars.name: PUSH_CALL_TO
vars.prompt: Recipient E.164 (omit to use the Worker's USER_CELL_E164 default)

verify.cmd: python seneschal/scripts/push_call.py --env-file {path} --text "Setup verify: this is a dry run." --dry-run

entries.title: Outbound SMS pushes (via the call-screener Worker)
entries.enable_question: Enable SMS pushes for brief highlights (requires the phone/ call-screener Worker deployed)?

depends.why: the Worker endpoint must exist and PUSH_SMS_SECRET must be set on it (wrangler secret put) before this env can work

notes: If the Worker isn't deployed yet, mark this chapter blocked and move on — deploying the Worker is its own task, not an inline step of the env walker.
Twilio creds stay in Cloudflare; only the Worker URL + bearer secret live here.
Verify is a --dry-run (no network, no send); a live test SMS is owner-initiated.

vars.name: PUSH_SMS_URL
vars.prompt: Full endpoint URL of the deployed Worker (include /push-sms)

vars.name: PUSH_SMS_SECRET
vars.prompt: The bearer secret matching `wrangler secret put PUSH_SMS_SECRET` on the Worker

vars.name: PUSH_SMS_TO
vars.prompt: Recipient E.164 (omit to use the Worker's USER_CELL_E164 default)

verify.cmd: python seneschal/scripts/push_sms.py --env-file {path} --text "Setup verify: this is a dry run." --dry-run

entries.title: Seneschal Cockpit OIDC auth (optional — dev-no-auth is the default)
notes: Owned by the cockpit chapter (handled_by: cockpit) — listed here so the doctor sees every env surface.

Dev-no-auth remains the default: leave COCKPIT_OIDC_CLIENT_ID unset until the OIDC app is provisioned (cockpit/zitadel/ZITADEL_SETUP.md); setting it flips auth_mode() to 'oidc' and turns on the real login round trip.
The session-cookie signing secret is deliberately NOT an env var — auto-generated to state/cockpit-session-secret.

vars.name: COCKPIT_OIDC_ISSUER
vars.prompt: The OIDC provider's issuer URL (discovery finds the rest)

vars.name: COCKPIT_OIDC_CLIENT_ID
vars.prompt: The cockpit's OIDC client id (PKCE public client; leave unset for dev-no-auth — provisioning: cockpit/zitadel/ZITADEL_SETUP.md)

vars.name: COCKPIT_OIDC_REDIRECT
vars.prompt: Registered redirect URI (must match the OIDC app exactly)

vars.name: COCKPIT_ALLOWED_USER
vars.prompt: The single allowed cockpit username

entries.title: Slack MCP config (daemon Slack send hands)
notes: A JSON MCP config, not an env file (format: json) — the mcp chapter owns writing it; listed here for doctor completeness.
Auto-detected by presence.py once present (--no-slack disables).
entries.vars_incomplete_reason: JSON MCP config — KEY=VALUE var parity does not apply; the mcp chapter validates its shape.

entries.title: Notion MCP config (store backend + headless daemon Notion access)
notes: A JSON MCP config, not an env file (format: json) — the mcp chapter owns writing it; listed here for doctor completeness.
Only relevant on the notion store backend; filesystem backends need no MCP.
Needs a one-time OAuth + daemon restart before headless writes work.
